Voice typing is reliable: it waits for your last words, types into the field you're in and then gives your clipboard back, and the AI polish actually runs on macOS. Esc cancels a dictation, Parley can start at login, and a report that used to sit at "Analyzing 0/4" now finishes or tells you why.

**Voice typing** (#567, thanks to @ncchen99)

- Quick taps and releasing on the last word no longer drop text: Parley waits for the recognizer's final answer before it pastes.
- Your clipboard is yours again. Parley pastes the dictation and puts back what you had copied a moment later — unless you copied something new in the meantime. Clipboard managers and Windows clipboard history skip the dictation, and password-manager entries are never read.
- In Remote Desktop, virtual machines and other remote sessions, the dictation is pasted and left on the clipboard so it reaches the remote side.
- AI polish runs on macOS (it silently failed before). Very short and one-clause dictations skip it, so they paste instantly. Tidy and Concise work as before.
- Press Esc while dictating to cancel; Undo puts the text on the clipboard and in history.
- Pauses no longer leave a 。 in the middle of a sentence; a one-clause dictation drops its trailing 。.
- Your name, company and dictionary help recognition and polish, and edits to the dictionary apply right away.
- The overlay no longer steals focus from the app you're typing in, and its empty areas pass clicks through (macOS). ⌥↩ no longer starts push-to-talk.
- The pill says "Inserted" and has a Copy button; the History tab updates on its own.

**Launch at login** (#567)

- Settings › Basic › Launch at login. Parley starts hidden in the menu bar / tray.

**Reports don't get stuck** (#590)

- A stage whose model call stalls now gives up and shows "the model took too long" instead of "Generating" forever, and you can regenerate a stage while it is still running.
- Slow and reasoning models get room to think before their first words, so long meetings still finish.
- Findings cited past 100 minutes land at the right moment (#591).

**Replay audio** (#590)

- If a recording won't play, Parley converts it and plays that instead; if that fails too, the player says why. A recording with no audio on this computer says so instead of showing a dead play button.
- Switching recordings while one is being converted no longer plays the wrong audio.
